ideas.title: Ask a question, get a partition: criterion-conditioned MI clustering with retrieval-derived gene weights
ideas.one_line: The user gives a free-text criterion such as "type I interferon response" or "immune lineage". Retrieval turns literature gene mentions into cited gene weights, and a weighted MI (NVI) distance makes MICA return the partition that answers that question. The benchmark uses datasets with several orthogonal ground-truth label sets.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
- **MICA has one fixed view.** It uses every gene as an equal sample in cell-to-cell MI and argues against HVG selection. So its single partition follows the strongest structure, usually lineage. To cluster by stimulation, drug response or cell cycle, a user has to pick a gene set by hand and recluster. The partition cannot be steered or audited.
- **Text-steered "multiple clustering" is active in vision only.** Examples: IC|TC (Kwon et al., arXiv:2310.18297, reported as ICLR 2024, venue UNVERIFIED), Multi-MaP (CVPR 2024, arXiv:2404.15655), Multi-Sub (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2411.03978) and Multi-DProxy (AAAI 2026, arXiv:2511.07274). An arXiv API query today for clustering with user or text criteria found no gene expression or biology version.
- **Single-cell knowledge priors are fixed programs, not free-text criteria.** PAGODA (Nat Methods 2016, https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.3734), Spectra (Nat Biotechnol 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01940-3) and expiMap (Nat Cell Biol 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41556-022-01072-x) all work this way.
- **Text-cell joint spaces score cells but do not build criterion-conditioned partitions with cited features.** CellWhisperer (Nat Biotechnol 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-025-02857-9) and LangCell (ICML 2024, arXiv:2405.06708) are examples.
- **Europe PMC check today.** A query for LLM or retrieval steering how cells are clustered (2024 to 2026) returned only annotation and gene-set tools. Examples: ELISA (Brief Bioinform 2026, https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbag501) and knowledge-guided contextual gene set analysis (Bioinformatics 2026, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btag214, details UNVERIFIED).
- **Why MICA's machinery carries over.** Normalized variation of information is a metric (Vinh et al., JMLR 2010, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/vinh10a/vinh10a.pdf). A weighted gene measure is still a probability space, so the weighted NVI should stay a metric. This is my derivation and needs checking.
ideas.method_sketch:
1. **Criterion to evidence.** Hybrid BM25 plus MedCPT retrieval over PubMed abstracts and PMC OA passages (MedCPT: Bioinformatics 2023, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btad651, with NCBI precomputed PubMed embeddings at https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/lu/MedCPT/pubmed_embeddings/, full coverage not confirmed). An optional local LLM writes query expansions (HyDE-style).
2. **Evidence to gene relevance model.** Take PubTator3-normalized gene mentions from the top-k passages (NAR 2024, https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkae235). Score genes by retrieval score times inverse document frequency, in the spirit of RM3. Keep passage IDs as per-gene citations.
3. **Pseudo-relevance feedback in expression space.** Add genes that are strong MI neighbors of top-weighted genes in this dataset, using scMINER's SJARACNe network or a cheap gene-gene MI. Drop genes with no variation.
4. **Weighted MI distance.** Joint histogram cells become sums of gene weights, and D_w = 1 - I_w/H_w. The simple variant is a hard top-m gene subset. MICA's per-cell binning is kept.
5. **Cluster.** Use MICA-MDS (small data) or MICA-GE (large). An optional nuisance criterion down-weights genes retrieved for a second criterion, for example lineage.
6. **Output.** The partition, the gene weights, and the passages behind the top genes. An optional second view is scMINER driver activity limited to retrieved regulators.
- **Course MVP by December:** hard-subset variant on all three datasets. **Paper:** soft weights, PRF, full baselines and a citation study.
ideas.experiments:
**Datasets.** Each has at least two orthogonal label sets, mostly non-circular.
- **D1 (≥5,000 × ≥20): Bodenmiller_BCR_XL CyTOF.**
  - 172,791 cells and 24 protein markers: 10 lineage markers classed "cell type" and 14 signaling markers classed "cell state". 8 paired samples of BCR-XL stimulated vs reference PBMC.
  - Population labels come from FlowSOM plus expert merging (HDCytoData reference manual, https://bioconductor.org/packages/HDCytoData).
  - Criteria: "immune lineage" vs "BCR/Fc receptor signaling". The type/state marker classes are ground truth for whether retrieval weighted the right features.
  - With 24 features MICA gets floor(24^(1/3)) = 2 bins, so also report weighted Euclidean on arcsinh data as the low-dimension adaptation.
- **D2 (≥2M × ≥10): a 2M-cell slice of Tahoe-100M** (https://huggingface.co/datasets/tahoebio/Tahoe-100M, CC0).
  - Labels: SNP-demultiplexed cell line (Cellosaurus ID), drug, fine MoA, plate.
  - Criteria: "cell line or tissue of origin" vs strong MoAs such as proteasome or MEK inhibition. Build the slice from drugs with clear transcriptional effects.
  - Backup: Allen WMB 10Xv3, region vs class.
- **D3 (≥500 × ≥700): Kang 2018 IFN-beta PBMC** (GSE96583, Nat Biotechnol 2018, https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042).
  - About 29K cells before QC, 8 genotype-demultiplexed donors, stim vs control, cell type labels. Counts UNVERIFIED.
  - Criteria: "interferon response" vs "immune lineage".
  - Optional richer D3 or D2: Parse 10M PBMC, 90 cytokines, CC BY-NC, form download.

**Metrics**
- Target AMI and ARI against the label set the criterion names.
- Off-target AMI against the other label sets.
- Steerability = target AMI minus the largest off-target AMI.
- Gene-weight nDCG against reference sets: MSigDB Hallmark interferon sets, Tirosh cell-cycle genes, CyTOF marker classes.
- Citation support rate for top genes, judged by teammates.

**Baselines**
- Unweighted MICA.
- HVG plus PCA plus Leiden.
- Keyword lookup into MSigDB, no retrieval.
- LLM-only gene list from local Qwen3-32B, also counting hallucinated symbols.
- AUCell score of the retrieved set plus k-means (tests whether weighted MI adds anything beyond scoring).
- Spectra or expiMap factors plus clustering.
- CellWhisperer text-query similarity on the human datasets.
- An LLM agent (CellAgent- or Biomni-style) that picks genes and reclusters.

**Ablations:** soft vs hard weights, PRF on or off, BM25 vs dense vs hybrid, passage count, weighted MI vs weighted cosine.
ideas.compute_estimate:
All figures are estimates, not measurements.
- **PubMed index.** Built once and shared with the other RAG ideas.
  - BM25 over about 36M abstracts: 1 to 3 h on 120 cores.
  - MedCPT embeddings: about 110 GB float32 in the 754 GB RAM, or an IVF-PQ index of 5 to 10 GB.
- **Query expansion.** Qwen3-32B in BF16, tensor-parallel across both 48 GB GPUs with vLLM: minutes.
- **Weighted MI, small data.** Kang and CyTOF over a few hundred to a few thousand genes: minutes to about an hour on CPU.
- **Tahoe 2M slice.**
  - Streaming parquet download of tens of GB.
  - MI-kNN on ≤1,000 genes for 2M cells: several hours on 120 cores with hnswlib or pynndescent custom metrics, or a 200K sketch plus kNN propagation.
- **Training.** None. Fits within 12 h runs.

ideas.novelty_claim: The first single-cell clustering method where the partition is conditioned on a free-text criterion. It works through retrieval-derived, citation-backed gene weights inside a weighted mutual-information (NVI) distance extending MICA. It is benchmarked with a steerability metric on datasets with several orthogonal ground-truth labelings: genotype, stimulation and lineage.
ideas.closest_prior_work:
- **Vision multiple clustering:**
  - IC|TC (arXiv:2310.18297, 2023, ICLR 2024 UNVERIFIED)
  - Multi-MaP (CVPR 2024, arXiv:2404.15655)
  - Multi-Sub (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2411.03978)
  - Multi-DProxy (AAAI 2026, arXiv:2511.07274)
- **Knowledge gene programs:**
  - PAGODA (Nat Methods 2016, https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.3734)
  - Spectra (Nat Biotechnol 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01940-3)
  - expiMap (Nat Cell Biol 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41556-022-01072-x)
- **Text-cell models:**
  - CellWhisperer (Nat Biotechnol 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-025-02857-9)
  - LangCell (ICML 2024, arXiv:2405.06708)
  - scELMo (Patterns 2026, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patter.2025.101431)
- **Base method:** MICA/scMINER (Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6).
ideas.risks:
- **Biggest risk.** For well-studied criteria like interferon, "pick the MSigDB set and recluster" may match the method. The claim then has to rest on criteria without clean curated sets, on steerability and on citations, not on accuracy for easy criteria.
- **Agent baseline.** Agent systems can pick genes and recluster by writing code, and reviewers will ask for that baseline.
- **Estimator noise.** Weighted plug-in MI is noisy with few genes. On D1 (24 markers) MI is nearly degenerate, so D1 will likely show MI's limits rather than gains.
- **Tahoe slice design.** Cell lines separate trivially and many drugs have weak effects, so the slice must be chosen carefully.
- **Kang is too simple.** It has only two conditions, so steering toward stimulation is close to supervised. A richer criterion set (Parse 10M cytokines) would help but needs a form and has circular cell-type labels.
- **Scoop risk is moderate.** Text-conditioned clustering is active in vision, and LLM-for-single-cell work is crowded.

ideas.title: Two-key refinement of over-clustered MI graphs: held-out statistical separation plus retrieval-verified hidden-driver evidence, with attribution metrics
ideas.one_line: Over-cluster with MICA, then walk the merge tree. A boundary between sibling clusters is kept only if it separates on held-out data AND a local LLM finds retrieved literature supporting distinct identities or states. The evidence is built from held-out markers and scMINER hidden drivers, and every kept boundary gets a citation-faithfulness score.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
- **Regulator activity is unused as evidence.** No method found uses computed TF, regulon or driver activity (SCENIC, VIPER, NetBID, scMINER) as retrieval or LLM evidence (llm-rag sweep). A Europe PMC query today (LLM plus regulon, TF activity, master regulator or driver activity, 2024 to 2026) returned no such method. ScanNet (PLoS Comput Biol 2026, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014602) uses a regulatory network for annotation through graph learning, with no LLM or retrieval. Hidden drivers, which change in activity but not in expression, are invisible to every marker-based tool.
- **LLM feedback into clustering exists only in partial form.**
  - GPTAnno selects one resolution (bioRxiv 2025, https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.27.690951).
  - CellMaster suggests split or merge to a human (arXiv:2602.13346, 2026).
  - HypoGeneAgent scores resolutions for gene programs (arXiv:2509.09740, 2025).
  - None of them makes automatic pairwise decisions, controls double dipping, or runs on MI clustering.
- **Statistical merge methods explain nothing.** CHOIR (Nat Genet 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-025-02148-8), sc-SHC (Nat Methods 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01933-9) and recall (AJHG 2025) use no external knowledge and cannot say why a boundary matters.
- **scMINER's own tests have calibration problems.** Its differential activity tests reuse the cells that define the clusters, which is double dipping. The SJARACNe consensus p-value is miscalibrated according to the developers' draft PR #73 (Aug 2026, github.com/jyyulab/SJARACNe).
- **No claim-level attribution metrics.** No cell annotation paper measures citation precision or recall. "From Cluster to Claim" (Lin and Yu, Adv Genet 2026, https://doi.org/10.1002/ggn2.70045) calls for matching claim strength to evidence strength, but gives a framework, not a method.
ideas.method_sketch:
1. **Split.** Count-split the RNA into fold A (clustering) and fold B (evidence) (Neufeld et al., Biostatistics 2024, https://doi.org/10.1093/biostatistics/kxac047). For CITE-seq, cluster on ADT and use RNA as evidence, a cross-modal split.
2. **Over-cluster and build the tree.** Run MICA-GE at high resolution on fold A, then build a merge tree from inter-cluster connectivity in the MI-kNN graph.
3. **Per sibling pair, bottom-up, on fold B:**
   - (a) A CHOIR-style permutation test of classifier separability.
   - (b) Differential markers.
   - (c) Driver activity on metacells, then flag hidden drivers: significant differential activity with non-significant differential expression. Activity comes from scMINER SJARACNe networks per parent cluster with PR #73's recurrence rule, or from CollecTRI regulons (NAR 2023, https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkad841) plus decoupleR as the cheap default.
4. **Retrieval.**
   - Queries combine tissue context, markers and top differential drivers.
   - Corpus: PubMed abstracts, CellMarker 2.0 (NAR 2023, https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkac947) and Cell Ontology definitions.
   - BM25 plus MedCPT hybrid, then cross-encoder reranking.
5. **Verifier.** A local LLM (Qwen3-32B or gpt-oss-120b in vLLM) sees both evidence bundles. It answers {distinct identity, distinct state of same identity, same, insufficient}, and every claim must cite passage IDs. An NLI model checks each claim against its cited passage and removes unsupported ones.
6. **Two-key decision.** Keep the split only if the held-out test passes at FDR alpha AND supported evidence remains. Splits that rest only on hidden drivers get a stricter alpha. Otherwise merge and move up the tree.
7. **Output.** The final partition plus an evidence card for each kept boundary.
- **Course MVP by December:** D3 end to end with CollecTRI activity, plus D1. D2 at class and subclass level only.
ideas.experiments:
**Datasets**
- **D1 (≥5,000 × ≥20): Hao 2021 CITE-seq PBMC** (GSE164378, Cell 2021, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2021.04.048).
  - About 162K cells, clustered on 228 ADTs, with RNA as held-out evidence.
  - Labels l1, l2 and l3 come from WNN, so they are partly circular. Say so.
- **D2 (≥2M): Allen whole mouse brain 10Xv3** (2.3M cells × 32,285 genes, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06812-z).
  - Cluster a 200K sketch and propagate labels by kNN.
  - Score decisions at class, subclass and supertype level.
  - Build networks only for ≤100 candidate pairs, on metacells.
- **D3 (≥500 × ≥700):**
  - PBMC14K (13,605 × 17,986, FACS-sorted labels). Its Treg, CD4 memory and naive boundaries are where scMINER reports activity-based gains.
  - Zeisel 2015 (3,005 × 19,972, 47 subclasses, GSE60361).

**Null experiments**
- A single FACS-sorted population, and splatter-simulated one-type data. Every kept split there is false.
- Run each with and without count splitting to measure the effect of double dipping.

**Baselines**
- CHOIR, sc-SHC, recall, SCCAF and Cytocipher.
- Silhouette and modularity selection, and oracle K.
- GPTAnno and an automatic-mode CellMaster, both reimplemented with the same local LLM.
- CASSIA (Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67084-x) where it runs.

**Metrics**
- ARI, AMI, wNMI (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-020-02027-x) and LCAD (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-025-03781-6), all at each method's own K.
- Boundary precision and recall, where a boundary is true if the siblings map to different reference labels.
- Rare-type F1, and false-split rate on the null data.
- Attribution:
  - Citation precision and recall (ALCE, Gao et al., EMNLP 2023, arXiv:2305.14627).
  - Nugget recall of the evidence cards (AutoNuggetizer, Pradeep et al., arXiv:2411.09607, 2024).
  - Human judgments by teammates on about 300 claims, with inter-annotator agreement.

**Ablations**
- Markers only vs markers plus drivers, and SJARACNe vs CollecTRI.
- Retrieval off (LLM parametric knowledge only), LLM off (retrieval-score rule), NLI filter off.
- Open model vs one API model on a subset.
- A corpus with cell-type names masked, to measure reliance on names.
ideas.compute_estimate:
All figures are estimates.
- **Verifier LLM.** Qwen3-32B in BF16, tensor-parallel on 2×48 GB. About 2K to 5K calls at roughly 4K input tokens: 1 to 3 h.
- **NLI and cross-encoder reranking.** Under 1 h on one GPU.
- **Retrieval index.** Shared with the other RAG ideas: 1 to 3 h to build BM25, and about 110 GB RAM or an IVF-PQ index for MedCPT.
- **CollecTRI plus decoupleR activity.** Minutes.
- **SJARACNe.** The main cost.
  - Roughly 1 to 4 CPU hours per network on about 1,000 metacells with fewer bootstraps.
  - Memory needs capping. Issue #50 reports 160 to 200 GB for 1,361 cells on 32 cores.
  - Cap at 50 to 100 networks, run in the background over a few days.
- **MICA-GE on a 200K sketch.** A few CPU hours.
- **Allen raw download.** About 95 GB.
- **Training.** None.

This is the best fit of the four for Laraib and Rhea. They can own:

- The evidence-card rubric.

- Writing up the biology of the hidden-driver case studies.

Utshab owns splitting, retrieval, the vLLM verifier, the decision rule and the harness.
ideas.novelty_claim: The first automatic merge/split procedure for single-cell clustering where each boundary must pass two keys. One is held-out statistical separation, from a count split or a cross-modal split. The other is retrieval-verified evidence that includes network-inferred driver activity (hidden drivers). It is also the first to report claim-level attribution metrics for the evidence behind each kept boundary.
ideas.closest_prior_work:
- **LLM feedback into clustering:**
  - GPTAnno (bioRxiv 2025, https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.27.690951)
  - CellMaster (arXiv:2602.13346, 2026)
  - HypoGeneAgent (arXiv:2509.09740, 2025)
- **LLM annotation and verification:**
  - CASSIA (Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67084-x)
  - GeneAgent (Nat Methods 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-025-02748-6)
- **Statistical merge methods:**
  - CHOIR (Nat Genet 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-025-02148-8)
  - sc-SHC (Nat Methods 2023, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01933-9)
  - recall (AJHG 2025, DOI discrepancy noted in the resolution report)
- **Inference after clustering:** count splitting (Biostatistics 2024, https://doi.org/10.1093/biostatistics/kxac047).
- **Base method:** scMINER (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6).
- **Recent RAG work:** RAGCell (arXiv:2609.14147, posted 12 Sep 2026). It uses RAG as a training signal, not for clustering decisions.
ideas.risks:
- **Crowded area.** This is the most crowded of the four. GPTAnno or CellMaster could add pairwise decisions in a revision, and RAGCell appeared four days ago. The claim has to rest on the three parts with no prior found: driver evidence, held-out splitting and attribution metrics.
- **Many parts for one semester.** Keep the course scope to the MVP.
- **SJARACNe problems.** Install and runtime failures (issues #44, #50, #51, #52, #57) and a miscalibrated cutoff. Falling back to CollecTRI weakens the tie to scMINER.
- **Count-splitting assumptions.** It assumes Poisson or negative-binomial counts, so it is invalid for ADT or normalized data. Held-out folds halve the signal and hurt rare types.
- **Knowledge bias.** The knowledge key may merge real but unpublished populations. The null and name-masked experiments must bound this.
- **Human labels take time.** Attribution judgments need a clear rubric.
- **LLM nondeterminism.** Use temperature 0 and report variance over repeats.

ideas.title: Query performance prediction as a knowledge-grounded validity index for choosing MICA's k and resolution
ideas.one_line: Turn each cluster's held-out markers, and optionally its hidden drivers, into a literature query. Score how focused the retrieval is with null-calibrated QPP predictors. The partition-level score then picks MICA's k or Louvain resolution with no labels and no LLM generation.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
- **scMINER's accuracy numbers use an oracle** (deep read of Source Data and run scripts).
  - MDS mode set k to the true class count.
  - GE mode swept resolution until the cluster count matched the truth.
  - GE-mode ARI on Zeisel ranged from about 0.12 to 0.81 across resolutions.
  - The docs pick PBMC14K resolution 2.05 from prior knowledge.
- **Internal indices are unreliable here.** See the silhouette shortcomings (Rautenstrauch and Ohler, Nat Biotechnol 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-025-02743-4). Relative validity indices are also unsuitable for comparing similarity paradigms such as MI vs Euclidean (Yerbury et al., ACM TKDD 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10351).
- **Knowledge-guided selection so far needs repeated LLM generation and ignores double dipping.** Examples: GPTAnno (https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.27.690951) and HypoGeneAgent (arXiv:2509.09740).
- **Literature coherence has only been scored for gene groups, not cell partitions.** Raychaudhuri, Schütze and Altman (Genome Res 2002, https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.116402) and Raychaudhuri and Altman (Bioinformatics 2003, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btg002) did it for microarray gene clusters.
- **IR query performance prediction has not been used to judge clusterings.** Relevant predictors:
  - Clarity (Cronen-Townsend et al., SIGIR 2002, https://doi.org/10.1145/564376.564429)
  - NQC (Shtok et al., ACM TOIS 2012, https://doi.org/10.1145/2180868.2180873)
  - Dense coherence (Vlachou and Macdonald, arXiv:2310.11405, 2023)
  - Checks today: arXiv API queries for QPP with clustering, cluster validity or genes found nothing relevant. A Europe PMC query for literature-based selection of cell cluster number or resolution found nothing relevant. The search was limited, so novelty is likely but not certain.
ideas.method_sketch:
1. **Candidate partitions from MICA.** MDS mode with k from 2 to 40, GE mode with resolution from 0.1 to 4, and nested merges.
2. **Double-dipping control.**
   - Count splitting or data thinning (Biostatistics 2024, https://doi.org/10.1093/biostatistics/kxac047; JMLR 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.07276).
   - Cluster on fold A. Build each cluster's signature on fold B: top markers by AUROC, plus optional scMINER hidden drivers.
   - For CITE-seq, cluster on protein and build signatures from RNA.
3. **Query.** Gene symbols normalized to NCBI Gene IDs with synonyms, plus species and tissue terms.
4. **Retrieval.**
   - BM25 over PubMed abstracts (Pyserini) plus MedCPT dense retrieval using NCBI's precomputed article embeddings (https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btad651).
   - PubTator3 gene normalization to avoid ambiguous symbols (https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkae235).
   - Exclude the dataset's own source paper.
5. **Per-cluster predictors.**
   - Pre-retrieval: mean IDF and SCQ.
   - Post-retrieval: clarity against the collection model, NQC, WIG, and dense top-k coherence.
   - Concept focus: entropy of MeSH cell-type descriptors among the top-k documents.
6. **Null calibration (the key step).** z-score every predictor against random gene sets matched on size, expression level and literature frequency. This removes the plain popularity effect.
7. **Partition score and selection.** Size-weighted mean z minus a complexity penalty. Pick the smallest k or resolution within one SE of the best score.
8. **Pairwise merge signal.** Rank-biased overlap between sibling clusters' result lists (Webber, Moffat, Zobel, ACM TOIS 2010, https://doi.org/10.1145/1852102.1852106). High overlap suggests the same identity.
9. **Output.** The chosen partition plus the top supporting abstracts for each cluster. Everything is deterministic and needs no LLM.
- **Extension:** combine with a CHOIR-style held-out test as a two-key rule.
- **Course MVP by December:** BM25-only QPP on D3 and D1, with D2 on a sketch.
ideas.experiments:
**Datasets**
- **D1 (≥5,000 × ≥20): Hao 2021 CITE-seq ADT panel** (about 162K cells × 228 antibodies, l1/l2/l3 hierarchy, GSE164378).
  - Cluster on protein, with RNA as the held-out evidence modality.
  - Labels are WNN-derived, so state the circularity.
  - Levine_32dim CyTOF (265,627 × 32, 14 gated populations) serves as a small-vocabulary stress test.
- **D2 (≥2M): Allen WMB 10Xv3** (2.3M cells; 34 classes, 338 subclasses, 1,201 supertypes).
  - Which hierarchy level does the selector land on, and does it change by brain region?
  - MICA-GE runs on a 200K sketch with kNN propagation.
- **D3 (≥500 × ≥700):**
  - Zeisel (9 vs 47 labels).
  - PBMC14K (FACS labels).
  - Kolodziejczyk 2015 and Chu 2016 as low-literature controls (culture conditions and cell lines).

**Injected controls** that the index should penalize:
- Simulated doublet clusters.
- Low-quality and high-mito clusters.
- One cell type split artificially by donor or batch.

**Baselines**
- Oracle K, silhouette, modularity, gap statistic.
- scICE (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60702-8) and chooseR.
- CHOIR and sc-SHC.
- GPTAnno reimplemented with local Qwen3-32B.
- A Raychaudhuri-style literature coherence score.

**Metrics**
- Spearman correlation between per-cluster QPP z and per-cluster purity or F1.
- ARI, AMI and wNMI of the selected partition.
- Distance between the selected K and the label count at each hierarchy level.
- AUROC for flagging the injected artifact clusters.
- Runtime.

**Ablations**
- BM25 vs MedCPT vs hybrid.
- Null calibration on or off.
- Count split on or off, which measures double dipping directly.
- Markers only vs markers plus hidden drivers.
- A corpus with cell-type names masked.
- A temporal corpus cutoff (for example PubMed up to 2012), to test bias against types described later.
ideas.compute_estimate:
All figures are estimates.
- **BM25 index.** About 36M PubMed abstracts on 120 cores: 1 to 3 h, 30 to 60 GB disk.
- **MedCPT embeddings.** About 110 GB float32 held in RAM, or an IVF-PQ index of 5 to 10 GB. Query encoding on GPU is trivial.
- **Null distributions.** About 1e5 to 1e6 BM25 queries: a few CPU hours with cached postings.
- **MICA sweeps.**
  - D3 k grid in MDS mode: a few CPU hours. The Python MDS path is slow, 3,112 s on Klein per Source Data.
  - D2 resolution sweep in GE mode on a 200K sketch: several CPU hours in parallel.
- **Optional GPTAnno baseline.** Qwen3-32B on both GPUs: 1 to 3 h.
- **Training.** None. This is the lightest of the four ideas.

ideas.novelty_claim: The first use of null-calibrated query performance prediction over held-out cluster signatures as an internal validity index. It selects the number of clusters or the resolution for single-cell clustering (MICA MDS and GE modes) deterministically and without LLM generation. It includes explicit controls for double dipping and for literature popularity bias.
ideas.closest_prior_work:
- **Literature coherence of gene groups:**
  - Raychaudhuri et al. (Genome Res 2002, https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.116402)
  - Raychaudhuri and Altman (Bioinformatics 2003, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btg002)
- **LLM-based resolution selection:** GPTAnno (https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.27.690951) and HypoGeneAgent (arXiv:2509.09740).
- **Knowledge-graph convergence for annotation:** GATHER (SIGIR 2026, https://doi.org/10.1145/3805712.3809935).
- **Statistical selection:** CHOIR (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-025-02148-8) and sc-SHC (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01933-9).
- **Marker-based parameter tuning:** IKAP (GigaScience 2019, https://academic.oup.com/gigascience/article/8/10/giz121/5579995).
- **QPP:** clarity (https://doi.org/10.1145/564376.564429), NQC (https://doi.org/10.1145/2180868.2180873), dense coherence (arXiv:2310.11405).
ideas.risks:
- **Popularity confound.** Well-studied types retrieve focused results, while novel or rare types look incoherent. Null calibration may not fully remove this, and the index could bias against discovery. That would still be a finding worth reporting.
- **Weak signal.** QPP-to-effectiveness correlations in IR are usually moderate, so the per-cluster signal may be weak. No specific numbers were checked this session.
- **Artifact clusters may look coherent.** Stress, mitochondrial and cell-cycle clusters have focused literature too. The injected-control experiments must show whether this matters.
- **Sparse literature at fine levels.** Mouse brain supertypes have little literature, so the index may saturate at subclass level.
- **May lose to CHOIR on accuracy.** Then position it as a cheap, interpretable complement, or combine the two as a two-key rule.
- **Incremental novelty.** Reviewers may see it as incremental over Raychaudhuri 2003 unless the model-selection results are clearly better than silhouette and stability.

ideas.title: MI-RR: retrieve-then-rerank mutual information kNN graphs for atlas-scale MICA, with metric certificates and a first accuracy test at 2M cells
ideas.one_line: Treat MICA's MI distance as an expensive reranker. Generate candidates with a cheap proxy (PCA cosine or a distilled bi-encoder), rerank exactly with a GPU joint-histogram MI kernel, and certify kNN lists using the triangle inequality of normalized VI. This yields the first labeled accuracy evaluation of MI clustering at 2M+ cells.
ideas.problem_and_gap:
- **Scale.** MICA-GE's largest run was Covid650K: 13 h and 204 GB on 40 CPU cores, with no accuracy check (Pan et al. 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6, Supp. Fig. 4).
- **Code blocks larger runs.**
  - On `main` (checked today), `mica_ge.py` builds the MI graph with hnswlib (k=80, ef=400, M=8), CPU only.
  - The older `master` branch uses pynndescent with a numba MI metric instead. That explains the two reports' conflicting descriptions.
  - The deep read found a dense n × n adjacency (about 32 TB at 2M cells). Sparse fixes sit in the unmerged huge_dataset and huge_floating_k branches (PR #30).
- **No MI kNN graph above 1M objects anywhere.** Europe PMC and arXiv API checks today returned no relevant hits for cell-to-cell MI clustering at scale or on GPU. minicore reached 4M cells with JSD k-means, not MI (https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.03.24.436859).
- **Accuracy evidence stops at 13,605 cells** (PBMC14K). Skinnider et al. found MI weak among 17 measures (Nat Methods 2019, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0372-4). Whether MI helps at scale is untested.
- **The metric property is unused.** 1 - I/H(X,Y) is a true metric (Vinh et al., JMLR 2010, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/vinh10a/vinh10a.pdf), yet nobody has used it for pruning, certificates or sketch guarantees. The MDS path in code uses 1 - I/sqrt(H_i H_j), which is not a metric and differs from the paper (deep read, untested).
ideas.method_sketch:
1. **Pre-bin once.** Each cell gets uint8 bin codes using MICA's per-cell equal-width bins, with b = floor(G^(1/3)) by default. Store dense codes over the most-detected genes, or CSR codes of non-zero bins.
2. **First stage: candidate generation**, k' = 100 to 300, from either:
   - (a) PCA-50 cosine, or
   - (b) a small MLP bi-encoder distilled from exact MI with a MarginMSE-style loss on sampled triples (Hofstätter et al., arXiv:2010.02666).
   - Searched with FAISS or CAGRA on GPU (ICDE 2024, arXiv:2308.15136).
3. **Second stage: exact rerank.** Batched GPU joint histograms via bincount over b*x+y. Only genes non-zero in either cell are touched, and the (0,0) cell is filled by subtraction. Keep the top k by NVI.
4. **Certification.**
   - Choose L landmarks by farthest-first traversal in MI space and store D(x,l), for example 2.3M × 256 floats = about 2.4 GB.
   - Sort cells by D(.,l). The bound |D(x,l) - D(y,l)| ≤ D(x,y) limits unseen neighbors to a window.
   - A kNN list is certified exact when every cell in some landmark's window has been checked.
   - Report the certified fraction on sampled query cells, plus recall against exact MI on subsets.
   - This applies the bi-metric idea (Xu, Silwal, Indyk, arXiv:2406.02891, 2024) to MI.
5. **Clustering.** Symmetric kNN graph with similarity weights, which fixes MICA's use of distances as weights. Leiden via cuGraph or rapids-singlecell. MICA's node2vec step is kept as an ablation.
6. **Sketch mode for the course deadline.**
   - Farthest-first sketch in MI space, which inherits Hopper's 2-approximation Hausdorff guarantee because D is a metric (https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa408).
   - Cluster the sketch, then propagate labels by MI-kNN.
   - State a simple bound: a population whose MI separation exceeds twice the covering radius is guaranteed a representative.
7. **Estimator ablations on the fast kernel.** Zero-bin handling, quantile vs equal-width bins, Miller-Madow correction, NVI vs sqrt normalization.
ideas.experiments:
**Datasets**
- **D1 (≥5,000 × ≥20): Levine_32dim CyTOF** (265,627 × 32 markers, 14 gated populations, about 104K labeled; HDCytoData).
  - This is the breaking regime: b = floor(32^(1/3)) = 3 bins, and MI is estimated from 32 samples.
  - Compare equal-width, quantile and bias-corrected MI against Euclidean on arcsinh data and against FlowSOM. A negative result is expected and informative.
  - Hao 2021 ADT (about 162K × 228, b = 6) is the moderate-dimension check.
- **D2 (≥2M × ≥10): Allen WMB 10Xv3** (2.3M × 32,285 genes; class, subclass and supertype labels; public S3; CC BY-NC 4.0; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06812-z).
  - Those labels came from a PCA plus Leiden pipeline, which favors Euclidean methods.
  - Non-circular check: a 2M slice of Tahoe-100M with SNP-demultiplexed cell-line labels (CC0).
- **D3 (≥500 × ≥700): Zeisel 2015** (3,005 × 19,972, GSE60361).
  - Exact all-pairs MI is cheap here, and scMINER's published ARI of 0.744 is the anchor.
  - Chu 2016 and Kolodziejczyk 2015 form a small extra panel.

**Baselines**
- Shipped MICA-GE: document the failure at 2M, or run it on a 650K subsample.
- The MICA huge_dataset branch.
- rapids-singlecell or Scanpy PCA plus Leiden.
- SC3s (https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-022-05085-z).
- minicore JSD k-means.
- Seurat v5 sketch plus ProjectData.
- geosketch and Hopper in PCA space with kNN propagation.

**Metrics**
- Recall@k against exact MI on 50K-cell subsets, and the certified fraction.
- ARI and AMI at each label level, and wNMI (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-020-02027-x).
- Rare-type F1 for types below 0.1% of cells.
- Wall time, peak RAM and peak VRAM.
- Scores at a label-free resolution and at oracle K, reported separately.

**Ablations:** proxy type, k', number of landmarks L, sketch strategy (uniform vs PCA farthest-first vs MI farthest-first), binning rule, zero handling, distance vs similarity weights, Louvain vs Leiden, node2vec on or off.
ideas.compute_estimate:
All figures are estimates.
- **Memory.** Bin codes for 2.3M cells over about 8K genes: about 18 GB uint8 in RAM. Raw CSR: about 84 GB.
- **Proxy kNN.** 50-D search with FAISS or CAGRA: under 15 min on one RTX 6000 Ada.
- **Exact rerank.** 2.3M × 200 candidates × 8K genes on one GPU: about 1 to 3 h.
- **Landmark distances.** 2.3M × 256: under 1 h.
- **Distillation MLP.** 1 to 2 h on one GPU.
- **Leiden.** On about 50M edges: minutes on GPU, under 1 h on CPU.
- **Exact ground truth.** About 1 to 2 h per 50K-cell subset.
- **Totals.** The full pipeline fits one 12 h window. No LLM.
- **Download.** Allen raw data is about 95 GB, plus a Tahoe slice.

ideas.novelty_claim: The first kNN graph construction and clustering under a cell-to-cell mutual-information distance at ≥2M cells. It uses proxy retrieval plus exact MI reranking, with triangle-inequality certificates of kNN exactness and an MI-metric sketch with a rare-population coverage guarantee. It is also the first labeled accuracy benchmark of MI-based clustering above about 14K labeled cells, since scMINER reported only runtime at 650K.
ideas.closest_prior_work:
- **Base method:** MICA/scMINER (Nat Commun 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59620-6).
- **Proxy-plus-expensive-metric search:** bi-metric framework (Xu, Silwal, Indyk, arXiv:2406.02891, 2024, venue UNVERIFIED).
- **Information-theoretic clustering at scale:** minicore (bioRxiv 2021, https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.03.24.436859).
- **Sketching:** Hopper (Bioinformatics 2020, https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa408).
- **GPU single-cell pipelines:** rapids-singlecell (arXiv:2603.02402, 2026).
- **Distilling an expensive metric:**
  - Learning Wasserstein Embeddings (Courty et al., arXiv:1710.07457, ICLR 2018)
  - Cross-architecture ranking distillation (Hofstätter et al., arXiv:2010.02666, 2020)
- **GPU ANN:** CAGRA (ICDE 2024, arXiv:2308.15136).
ideas.risks:
- **MI may not beat PCA plus Leiden at scale** (see Skinnider 2019). The paper would then be a careful negative benchmark plus a fast tool: publishable but weaker.
- **Distance concentration.** Typical MI distances may bunch in a narrow range, which makes triangle-inequality windows loose and certificates rare. Measure this early on Zeisel.
- **Thin algorithmic novelty.** Bi-metric search, landmark pruning and farthest-first sketching are known, so reviewers may call it engineering.
- **Label problems.** Allen labels favor Euclidean pipelines, and Tahoe cell lines are too easy. Both are needed, and neither is perfect.
- **Distillation may add nothing** over PCA candidates. Report that honestly.
- **Scoop risk is low to moderate.** The MICA repo has branches named huge_dataset, distributed and arihantjain4-annoy-mi_knn, but no GPU or atlas-scale PR was visible today.
- **Weak link to RAG.** This idea has the weakest tie to the team's RAG motivation.

- IR framing: SIGIR 2027 short paper on bi-metric retrieval for scientific similarity functions (UNVERIFIED deadline).
- This idea can also serve as shared infrastructure for the other three.
